summary: The bill limits DC youth offender status to those under 18, requires the DC Attorney General to launch and maintain a public website with monthly updated juvenile arrest and prosecution statistics, and bars the DC Council from changing existing criminal sentences.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal or DC government spending, appropriations, or budgets. It focuses exclusively on criminal justice definitions, sentencing rules, and data reporting requirements.
No provisions address taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to healthcare systems, coverage, or policy.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration, borders, or related pathways/protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military or defense spending or policy.
No provisions address environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug decriminalization, enforcement, or related policies.

The bill directly amends DC criminal justice policy by narrowing the definition of 'youth offender' from age 24 to under 18, repealing provisions allowing sentences below mandatory minimums for this group, and mandating detailed public reporting on juvenile arrests and prosecutions. These changes shift policy toward stricter treatment of offenders aged 18-24 and greater transparency on crime statistics, aligning with tougher sentencing approaches.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions address foreign aid.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or related reforms.

The bill requires a public website with aggregated juvenile crime statistics but explicitly prohibits disclosure of personally identifiable information. This is a narrow transparency measure with no broader implications for tech regulation or privacy policy.
No provisions address labor, unions, or worker/employer policies.
No provisions address religious liberty, exemptions, or anti-discrimination laws.
